planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade; this old, narrow-leaved form of Japanese laurel is one of the most deep-shade-tolerant aucubas in the trade.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade, where it tolerates the deep, dry shade under mature trees better than almost any other broadleaf evergreen. Longifolia is an old, long-cultivated form of Japanese aucuba grown for its glossy, narrow, willow-like green leaves, giving it a finer, more graceful texture than the broad-leaved gold-dust forms. It needs only occasional grooming to remove winter-damaged leaves and tolerates salt spray, pollution, and heavy root competition.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade; this old female selection, which received an RHS First Class Certificate in 1865, needs a male aucuba nearby to set berries.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade, where its glossy, dark green leaves edged in soft yellow brighten dim corners year-round. Sulphurea Marginata is a long-grown female Japanese aucuba selection prized for its clean yellow leaf margin rather than the speckled blotching of 'Variegata' or 'Crotonifolia'; plant a male aucuba such as 'Golden King' nearby for its clusters of red winter berries. It tolerates dry shade, heavy clay, and root competition under large trees better than most broadleaf evergreens.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade; this Himalayan relative of the familiar Japanese aucuba shares its tolerance for deep, dry shade under trees.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade; Himalayan aucuba is a rounded evergreen shrub with long, narrow, glossy dark green leaves and toothed margins, native to dense forests and thickets on Himalayan slopes. Chartreuse spring flowers are followed by orange-red fruit on pollinated female plants. Like its better-known relative Aucuba japonica, it tolerates dry, deep shade, pollution, and salt wind better than almost any other broadleaf evergreen, making it useful for difficult shaded sites under established trees.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in well-drained, slightly acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade to morning sun; the white leaf margins blush pink in cool weather or strong sun.

directions: Plant in well-drained, slightly acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade to morning sun, sheltered from the hottest afternoon exposure. Tricolor is a slow-growing, spiny-leaved holly olive whose glossy green leaves are irregularly margined in white, with the margins taking on a pink or bronze blush in cold weather or bright light, giving year-round multicolor interest in a shaded border. Small, sweetly fragrant white flowers appear tucked among the foliage in fall. Little pruning is needed beyond light shaping after bloom.

common_name: Kaori Hime Osmanthus (Dwarf Fragrant Princess False Holly)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in well-drained, slightly acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade to partial sun; this extremely slow-growing dwarf selection stays compact for many years.

directions: Plant in well-drained, slightly acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade to partial sun. Kaori Hime (Japanese for 'fragrant princess') is a diminutive, extremely slow-growing holly olive selection with small, deep green, holly-like leaves, reaching only about 3 feet tall and 2 feet wide after many years. Its scented white flowers open among the foliage in fall like the species. Its tiny mature size makes it useful for small gardens, foundation plantings, and containers where a full-sized false holly would be too large.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in well-drained, humus-rich soil in full sun to partial shade; this selection reblooms through much of the year rather than only in fall.

directions: Plant in well-drained, humus-rich soil in full sun to partial shade. Semperflorens, also known as Sijigui or 'Four Seasons Osmanthus,' is a sweet olive selection with smooth, sparsely toothed leaves and pale yellow flowers that repeat every two to three months rather than blooming only in fall like the typical species, giving an extended season of its powerful apricot-like fragrance. It is reported to be among the more cold-hardy sweet olive forms. Little pruning is needed beyond light shaping to maintain a dense habit.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in well-drained sandy loam in full sun to partial shade, with afternoon shade in hot climates; native to dense Himalayan forest understories.

directions: Plant in well-drained sandy loam in full sun to partial shade, giving some afternoon shade in hot summer climates. Himalayan sweet osmanthus is a somewhat upright, leggier evergreen shrub than its relatives, with glossy dark green, serrate lanceolate leaves and clusters of intensely fragrant white, trumpet-shaped flowers in late winter to early spring rather than fall. Native to dense forests and thickets on Himalayan slopes, it brings off-season fragrance to the shrub border. Little pruning is needed beyond occasional shaping.
